issues.description: Class name mismatch between problem/template and the solution repository: the problem statement UML and the template Main refer to classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (and expect students to implement those). The solution repository, however, provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (and the files for Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java in the solution appear empty). This breaks naming consistency: the commented example code in Main (and the UML) refer to Seal/Pig/Goat, but the solution's concrete types have a different prefix. As a result the provided solution will not compile against the example/template usage and will confuse students about the expected class names and intended final API.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution repository's concrete animal class names match the problem/template expectations. Either (A) rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, and Goat (and update their constructors/implementations accordingly), or (B) add simple wrapper classes Seal, Pig, and Goat that delegate to the existing Space* implementations so the API (class names used in the UML and template Main) is present. Also ensure the example Main and commented examples reference the same class names. This preserves the intended exercise (students implement Seal/Pig/Goat) and avoids compilation/test harness failures.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (students are instructed to implement Seal, Pig, Goat). The solution repository instead provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This is a direct identifier mismatch for the same conceptual entities: students reading the problem/template expect classes named Seal/Pig/Goat, but the solution uses different class names. The difference also propagates to output strings (e.g., messageOnMilk/messageOnRide include the class name, so the solution will produce "SpaceSeal ... is milked" instead of the expected "Seal ... is milked"). This creates unnecessary cognitive overhead and makes it hard for students to map requirements to the provided solution (and will likely break tests or expectations that look for Seal/Pig/Goat).
issues.suggested_fix: Align class names across artifacts. Rename SpaceSeal -> Seal, SpacePig -> Pig, and SpaceGoat -> Goat in the solution repository (and update any references). Ensure messageOnMilk() and messageOnRide() produce the animal type matching the class names (e.g., "Seal [name] is milked" / "Riding on Seal [name]") — or, if the 'Space' prefix is intentional, update the problem statement and template to use the same 'Space' prefixed names so all artifacts are consistent.
